name: Practice (abhyāsa)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 7–9: The yoga of repeated practice (abhyāsa-yoga): with the mind yoked by it and not going to anything else, continually contemplating (anucintayan), one goes to the supreme divine Person (8.8).
signs_of_progress: result stated: one goes to the supreme divine Person (8.8)

name: Undivided devotion (ananya-bhakti)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 7–9: worship of the Lord with mind on nothing else — the knower 'of single devotion' (eka-bhakti, 7.17); constant remembrance with undivided mind (8.14); the supreme Person is attainable by undivided devotion (8.22); the great souls worship him with undistracted mind, knowing him as the imperishable origin of beings (9.13); for those who think of him with no other and worship him he carries gain and security (9.22); even one of very bad conduct who worships him with undivided devotion is to be deemed good, having resolved rightly (9.30); summed up in 9.34: mind on him, devoted to him, sacrificing to him, bowing to him, with him as the supreme aim.
signs_of_progress: quickly becomes righteous (dharmātman) and attains lasting peace (9.31)
the Lord bears his gain and security (9.22)

name: Remembering the Lord at the hour of death
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 7–9: at the time of the end, leave the body remembering the Lord alone (8.5); because one goes to whatever state one remembers at the end, having always been shaped by it, remember him at all times — for Arjuna, while fighting — with mind and intellect offered to him (8.6–7). The yogin's departure is described twice: with unmoving mind, devotion and the power of yoga, the breath made to enter between the brows (8.9–10); and with the gates restrained, the mind confined in the heart, the breath placed in the head, uttering Oṃ and remembering the Lord (8.12–13).

warnings.text: Whatever state one remembers when leaving the body, to that one goes (so the remembrance must be cultivated at all times).

prerequisites: lifelong remembrance, having 'always been shaped' by the state remembered (8.6–7, 8.14)
knowing the Lord with the adhibhūta, adhidaiva and adhiyajña (7.30)
signs_of_progress: result stated: one comes to the Lord's state / the supreme goal, without doubt (8.5, 8.7, 8.13)

name: Fixing the gaze or breath between the eyebrows (bhrū-madhya)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 8.10: at the time of departure the yogin, with steady mind, devotion and the power of yoga, makes the breath (prāṇa) enter fully between the brows and so reaches the supreme divine Person.

name: The vow of the brahmacārin (brahmacarya)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 7–9: Those who desire the imperishable practise brahmacarya (8.11).
notes: Named only as the discipline of those seeking the imperishable; no method given in this chunk.

name: Concentration (dhāraṇā)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 7–9: 'Established in yoga-dhāraṇā': restraining all the gates, confining the mind in the heart and placing the breath in the head at departure (8.12).

name: Offering all actions to the Lord (mad-arpaṇa)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 9.27–28 (with 8.7): whatever one does, eats, offers in the fire, gives or performs as austerity is to be done as an offering to the Lord; thus one is released from the bonds of action with their good and bad fruits and, with the self yoked in the yoga of renunciation, freed, comes to him; mind and intellect offered to him.
signs_of_progress: release from the bonds of action with auspicious and inauspicious fruits (9.28)

name: The sacrifice of knowledge (jñāna-yajña)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 7–9: Some worship the Lord by sacrificing with the sacrifice of knowledge — as one, as distinct, in many ways — him who faces in all directions (9.15).
notes: Chapter 9 names the practice without further method; its other Gītā occurrences lie outside this chunk.

name: Singing the Lord's names (kīrtana, nāma-saṅkīrtana)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 7–9: The great-souled always glorify the Lord (kīrtayantaḥ), striving, firm in vows, bowing with devotion, ever yoked (9.14).
stage: as practised by the great souls (mahātman, 9.13–14)

name: Bowing to the Lord (namaskāra)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 9.14, 9.34: bowing to the Lord with devotion as part of the great souls' worship; enjoined in the closing verse of ch. 9, 'bow to me' (māṃ namaskuru).
signs_of_progress: result stated with 9.34: 'you will come to me alone'

name: Offering a leaf, flower, fruit or water with devotion
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 7–9: Offer the Lord with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water; what is so offered by one whose self is pure/controlled he partakes of (9.26).
prerequisites: a self that is pure or restrained (prayatātman)

name: Meditation on Om (praṇava-upāsanā)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 7–9: Uttering 'Oṃ, the one-syllabled Brahman' while remembering the Lord as one leaves the body (8.13).

name: Taking refuge in the Lord alone (śaraṇāgati)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 7.14, 7.19, 7.29; 9.32: those who take refuge in the Lord alone (mām eva prapadyante) cross over his guṇa-made māyā; the knower takes refuge after many births, knowing 'Vāsudeva is all'; taking refuge in him, people strive for release from old age and death; whoever takes refuge in him — even those of sinful birth, women, vaiśyas and śūdras — reaches the highest goal.
signs_of_progress: reaching the highest goal, for anyone who takes refuge, even those of sinful birth, women, vaiśyas and śūdras (9.32)
notes: Chs. 7–9 contribution, combining extractor B's prc:saranagati and extractor A's prc:prapatti.

name: Constant remembrance of the Lord (smaraṇa)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 8.7–8, 8.14; 9.22, 9.34: remember the Lord at all times while doing one's duty ('remember me and fight'); with a mind yoked by the yoga of repeated practice (abhyāsa-yoga), going nowhere else, continually contemplate the supreme Person; remember him constantly, day after day, with mind on nothing else — for such an ever-yoked yogin he is easy to reach; think of him with no other; 'be one whose mind is on me'.
signs_of_progress: the Lord becomes 'easy to attain' (sulabha) for the constantly remembering yogin (8.14)

name: Yogic departure at death
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 7–9: Summary of the Gītā's account only: at the time of departure, with unmoving mind, devotion and the power of yoga, the breath is settled between the brows (8.10); the gates (of the body) are restrained, the mind confined in the heart, the breath placed in the head, and, established in yogic concentration (yoga-dhāraṇā), one utters Oṃ, remembers the Lord and leaves the body, going to the supreme goal (8.12–13). The Gītā gives no further method.
prerequisites: a mind trained by repeated practice (8.8)
signs_of_progress: result stated: he reaches the supreme divine Person / the supreme goal (8.10, 8.13)
notes: Restricted: summary only (config/data_model.md §6). The Gītā gives no further method, no measures and no warnings for it; none are added here. Chs. 7–9 contribution, combining extractor B's entry and extractor A's prc:gita-yogic-departure.
